name: Hōkūleʻa sails to Tahiti
traveler: The crew of the Hōkūleʻa, navigated by Mau Piailug
summary: A double-hulled voyaging canoe sails 4,000 kilometres from Hawaiʻi to Tahiti with no instruments, steered by the stars, swells and birds by a master navigator from Satawal in Micronesia. It answers those who said Polynesians could only have reached their islands by drifting, and starts a revival of voyaging across the Pacific.

stops.note: The canoe leaves Maui on 1 May.
Through the calms near the equator, where the stars are the only guide.
Terns lead them to the first atoll of the Tuamotus.
Seventeen thousand people meet the canoe on 4 June.
